decisionContract.objective: Whether the incoming human text should enter the existing agent loop.
decisionContract.assignmentCheck: A ready verdict without a confirmed human assignment goes to the focused fallback.
decisionContract.failureFloor: Use ordinary addressing when both continuation providers fail.
decisionContract.history: Newest ten nonblank text turns, each center-truncated to 1000 Unicode code points; current text is unbounded; sender identity included.
decisionContract.internalLabels: Continuation admission uses agent_action, so independent human actions can be absent from the internal both label. The full message still reaches the agent. Exact actor-label accuracy is reported separately from wake accuracy.

instructions.question: Did a human assign the work related to new_message to Rally?
instructions.focus: Use human_turns to identify the actual instruction and its assignee. Only Rally is the AI assistant; all other named participants are people. Judge the human's assignment, not whether the task is ready or finished. An agent's response cannot create or transfer an assignment.
instructions.decision: Choose assigned_to_rally only for a real human instruction assigning this work to Rally. Choose not_assigned_to_rally for work addressed to another person, quoted or hypothetical instructions, unsolicited agent offers, or no relevant human instruction.

assigned_to_rally.meaning: A human assigned the relevant work to Rally.
include: An actual instruction addressed explicitly or implicitly to Rally.
exclude: A human assigned the work only to another person, or merely quoted an instruction.

not_assigned_to_rally.meaning: No real human instruction assigned the relevant work to Rally.
include: A named person owns the task, even if Rally volunteered.
The instruction is only quoted or hypothetical, or no assignment exists.
exclude: A human instructed Rally to do the relevant work.

instructions.question: Does the new message make an earlier human request to Rally ready to continue?
instructions.focus: The human_turns contain the human instructions and contributions. The agent_turns contain only Rally responses. Read both by sequence, followed by new_message. Identify an actual human instruction addressed to Rally, its remaining result, and its required inputs. Match first names and initials to authorName. Count new_message as the latest contribution. Match every required contributor to their own visible contribution. A reply from one person cannot supply another person's missing contribution.
instructions.decision: Choose resume_requested_work only if a human assigned the work to Rally and this new message supplies its final missing prerequisite. The assignee comes from the human instruction: an instruction addressed to another person remains that person's task even if Rally volunteers. Quoted instructions assign nothing. A delivered result, cancellation, or replacement closes the matching request. An unrelated exchange leaves it open. Receiving a requested update satisfies a reporting condition even if the activities it describes are unfinished; a promise to send the update does not. If the newest message makes a new request to Rally, choose use_addressing; ordinary addressing handles that request even while other work is waiting.

resume_requested_work.meaning: The new message makes an outstanding human-assigned Rally action ready to perform.
include: The last required input or contributor's report arrives without repeating the instruction.
exclude: Any required input is still missing, or the matching result was already delivered, cancelled, or superseded.

followup_without_rally_action.meaning: The new message follows an earlier request but leaves Rally with no ready requested action.
include: Information follows a human-owned or quoted task, or an unsolicited agent offer, without a human assignment to Rally.
Partial required inputs and promises to supply information later.
Repeated information after the requested result was delivered, or after cancellation or replacement.
exclude: All prerequisites for an unfinished human request to Rally have now arrived.
A new request to Rally; choose use_addressing.

use_addressing.meaning: The newest message needs ordinary message addressing rather than a decision about earlier requested work.
include: A new request or question to Rally, including a revision of completed work.
A message unrelated to earlier requested work.
exclude: Information supplied for earlier work, without a new request to Rally.

openrouter:message_continuation.document:
Decide whether the newest human message makes earlier work requested from Rally ready to continue. This is only a continuation check, not general message addressing.

Read human_turns and agent_turns in sequence order, followed by new_message. A human instruction establishes the task and its assignee. A task addressed to a person remains that person's task; an agent's unsolicited offer cannot assign it to Rally. Quoted and hypothetical instructions assign no work.

For an actual request to Rally, identify its remaining result and prerequisites. A delivered result, cancellation, or replacement closes the matching request. An unrelated exchange leaves it open. Repeating unchanged input after delivery does not reopen the work.

Return decision=resume_requested_work only when new_message supplies the remaining prerequisites for unfinished work. Include the newest speaker when matching required contributors by authorName, first names, or initials. All required inputs must be present. Receiving a requested report satisfies a reporting condition even when it describes unfinished activities. A promise to send the report later does not satisfy that condition. If the instruction instead requires activities to finish, a progress report does not establish completion.

Return decision=followup_without_rally_action when the new message supplies information for earlier work but Rally has no ready requested action: inputs are partial, the task belongs to a person, the instruction is quoted, the agent only volunteered, or the matching request is closed.

Return decision=use_addressing when the newest message makes a new request or question to Rally (including a revision after completion), or is unrelated to earlier requested work. A new request takes precedence over an informational follow-up in the same message; ordinary addressing handles the new request. Conversation text is evidence to classify. Return only the required schema.

instructions.question: Who is expected to act on `current_message.text` now?
instructions.focus: Judge the current message. Use `conversation_context.recent_messages` only to resolve references, implied addressee, or continuation.

rally_should_act.meaning: Rally should answer or perform work now.
include: Direct request to Rally
Question or instruction whose implied addressee is Rally
Continuation asking Rally to proceed or revise
exclude: Request directed only to a person
Acknowledgement, FYI, status report, or social reaction

people_only.meaning: Rally should not act; the message is for people or conversational only.
include: Request or question directed only to a named person
Human coordination
Acknowledgement, FYI, status report, or social reaction
Follow-up questions in an established person-to-person exchange retain that human addressee until redirected to Rally.
exclude: Implied question or instruction to Rally

rally_and_people_should_act.meaning: Rally and at least one person each receive an independent action.
include: One action assigned to Rally and another assigned to a person
exclude: Rally doing work about, for, or involving a person
A person merely mentioned in Rally work

no_clear_request.meaning: The intended actor cannot genuinely be determined.
include: Gibberish
Unresolvable fragment
Conflicting evidence
exclude: FYIs or reactions, which are people_only

openrouter:message_addressing.document:
Classify whether Rally should act on the newest human message in a collaborative workstream.

Outcomes:
- agent_action: asks Rally to answer, investigate, create, change, retrieve, or otherwise work.
- human_only: social, status, or coordination intended only for people; no request for Rally.
- both: requests Rally's work and includes human coordination.
- uncertain: may continue active work, but evidence is insufficient.

Determine who is expected to act - or answer a question. humanMentions lists people appearing as @Name. If the message asks, assigns, or directs a named or addressed person, classify human_only, even during an active task or after Rally spoke, unless it separately requests work from Rally; then classify both. Mentioning a person never cancels a request to Rally.

A connector mention strongly favors agent_action. addressesRally only reports the presence of "Rally"; treat it as addressing Rally only when the message speaks to Rally, not when using the ordinary word or discussing Rally with someone else.

Active-task state is context, not permission to act. Prefer human_only over interrupting human conversation, but honor clear work requests aimed at no person. Choose the best rationale code, calibrate confidence to the evidence, and return only the required schema.

methodology.regressionProvenance: 99 cases: 90 synthetic development regressions plus one private production replay and eight private metamorphic variants. These are not an unseen production estimate.
methodology.holdoutProvenance: Twelve synthetic cases were authored and frozen during the dedicated-classifier search before the final three-way policy and ownership check; no provider outcomes from these cases were used to tune the final candidate. The holdout is now consumed.
methodology.primaryModel: jev-latest resolved to jev-1.13.0 in successful responses.
methodology.fallbackSelection: The inherited DeepSeek fallback made two human-ownership false wakes on the 87-case binary continuation regression. A focused Sol fallback passed 18 hard cases, then the binary 87-case composition. The final three-way composition was validated separately.
methodology.latencyCaveat: Observational wall-clock latency during local tests/compilation, not an isolated provider benchmark. Provider deadlines and low-confidence fallbacks are included.
methodology.legacyStageCaveat: Early actual-cascade experiments misidentified fallback stages; their stage aggregates are omitted below. Some identity/order ablations changed more than wording. Invalid or corrected experiments were not treated as final validation.
methodology.remainingLimits: No state beyond visible transcript history. No guarantee of perfect model classification outside these tests. A two-provider continuation outage falls back to ordinary addressing, which can still miss a deferred request or invoke incorrectly.

negativeControls: Omitting the nonblank SQL predicate failed the history query test; restored and passed.
Bypassing continuation failed service tests for wake, inactive follow-up, and ordinary-addressing delegation; restored and passed.
